resources.string: Why SINR is unavailable
Not camped on a cellular network, so there is no SINR to read
Missing the Phone state permission (READ_PHONE_STATE); the system refuses to report signal strength
Missing the Precise location permission (ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION); cell info cannot be read (required on Android 12+)
System location services are off; Android 12+ does not allow reading cell info
The current LTE cell does not report rssnr (SINR); this cell or firmware provides no quality reading
The current NR cell does not report ssSinr; this cell or firmware provides no 5G SINR
This device model or the current network mode does not report SINR (some ROMs block the field)

Criteria (values in effect)
These are the rules actually in effect. They follow any change on the Features page immediately, and can only be viewed, not edited.
① Fake full bars downgrade: RSRP ≥ %1$d dBm and (Ping > %2$d ms or SINR < %3$d dB%4$s)
, or ping fails completely
Applies when: RSRP is above %1$d dBm, that is, the signal bars look full. Criteria: Ping > %2$d ms or SINR < %3$d dB — matching either one counts as full bars without quality, and drops to 4G.
② Weak signal downgrade: RSRP < %1$d dBm
② Weak signal downgrade: off, not part of the decision

The two RSRP thresholds are mutually exclusive: the weak signal threshold must be at least 1 dBm below the strong signal threshold. If the values do not satisfy this, the sliders keep your numbers while the effective values converge automatically — the values shown on this page are the ones in effect.
Applies when: RSRP is below %1$d dBm. Strength only, independent of Ping and SINR; weak 5G is often slower and more power-hungry than stable 4G.
③ No downgrade: when neither rule is met, the current network mode is kept and nothing is changed.

%1$d consecutive healthy rounds are required to restore: a single healthy round may just be jitter, and switching network modes both drains power and risks dropping the connection. It also does not restore for %2$s after a downgrade, so it does not jump straight back to 5G.
